designs.label: Tartan band
designs.layout: A broad band down the engine cover woven from crossing stripes over the second colour, with thin accent sett lines.
designs.after: Stewart SF01 (1997), the Stewart Racing tartan band

designs.label: Deck split
designs.layout: A level split, one colour per deck, with a double pinline on the seam (accent stripe plus a fine second line).
designs.after: Lotus 49B Gold Leaf (1968), red over white with gold

designs.label: Bordered stripe
designs.layout: One centre stripe with a keyline each side in the second colour and a body-colour gap between.

designs.label: Tricolour sweep
designs.layout: Three equal raked bands across the rear half: first colour, accent, second colour.
designs.after: Alpine A521 (2021) launch livery, flag stripes across the rear

designs.label: Spearhead
designs.layout: One arrow along the car: a broad head at the front of the cover and a level shaft behind it, keylined in the second colour.
designs.after: Brabham BT52 (1983), a two-colour block scheme drawn to read on TV
refs: Motor Sport: Peter Stevens on his liveries

rounds.changed: First round: five new cover layouts added to the SPINE TOP design picker (wrap placement so the art reaches both cover flanks), each shot on TLX in McLaren and Williams colours, front three-quarter and side. Before publishing, spearhead was reshaped from a raked wedge to a level-shafted arrow because it read like the tricolour on the flank. Known weak spots: on McLaren colours, bordered stripe and spearhead barely show because both pattern colours sit close to papaya, and spearhead vs bordered stripe is the least distinct pair (29.7% of the paint area). Round 2 target: give the stripe and arrow a contrast colour that is guaranteed to stand off the body.
